{{Short description|Genus of ceratopsian dinosaurs}} {{Automatic taxobox | fossil_range = [[Late Cretaceous]], {{fossilrange|Maastrichtian|Maastrichtian|[[Maastrichtian]]}} | image = Ferenceratops dentary.jpg | image_caption = Holotype {{dinogloss|dentary}} seen from above and the right side | taxon = Ferenceratops | authority = [[Susannah Maidment|Maidment]] et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | type_species = {{extinct}}'''''Zalmoxes shqiperorum''''' | type_species_authority = Weishampel et al., [[2003 in paleontology|2003]] }} '''''Ferenceratops''''' is an [[extinct]] genus of [[ceratopsia]]n dinosaurs known from the [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Maastrichtian]]) [[Sânpetru Formation|Sânpetru]] and [[Densuș-Ciula Formation|Densuș-Ciula]] formations of [[Romania]]. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Ferenceratops shqiperorum''''', known from a partial skeleton and [[pelvis]]. These fossils, in addition to many other isolated or associated remains, were originally referred to the {{gloss|[[rhabdodontid]]}} [[ornithopod]] ''[[Zalmoxes]]''. [[Phylogenetic analyses]] based on new remains of ''[[Ajkaceratops]]'' suggest ''Ferenceratops'' was a close relative of this genus, as part of a distinct lineage of previously unrecognized European ceratopsians. == History == [[File:Zalmoxes shqiperorum.jpg|thumb|left|Reconstructed skeleton based on the original [[iguanodont]] classification, [[Musee d'Histoire Naturelle, Brussels]]]] In 2003, [[David B. Weishampel]] and colleagues described the new genus ''[[Zalmoxes]]'' based on fossil material found in many [[Maastrichtian]]-aged localities throughout the [[Hațeg#Geology|Hațeg Basin]] of [[Transylvania]], Romania. Using this material, the authors recognized [[Rhabdodontidae]] as a new [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] of [[iguanodontia]]n [[ornithopod]] dinosaurs, also including the genus ''[[Rhabdodon]]''. Weishampel et al. established ''Zalmoxes robustus'' as the [[type species]], which had previously been placed in the genera ''[[Mochlodon]]'' and ''Rhabdodon''. They further named ''Z. shqiperorum'' as a new species in the genus ''Zalmoxes'', based on remains from the [[Sânpetru Formation]] previously identified as "''M.''"or "''R."'' ''robustus''. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]] honors the people of [[Shqiperia]], which is the name used by Albanians for their nation. {{gloss|Shqiperia}} is likely derived from the [[Albanian language|Albanian]] word {{lang|sq|shqipe}}, meaning {{gloss|eagle}}, in turn becoming {{gloss|shqipria}}, or {{gloss|land of the eagle}}. The [[holotype]] specimen of this species, housed at the [[Natural History Museum, London|Natural History Museum]] in [[London]], England as NHMUK PV R 4900, is a partial skeleton, including an incomplete right {{dinogloss|dentary}} and {{dinogloss|dorsals|dorsal (trunk) vertebra}}, left {{dinogloss|scapula}} and {{dinogloss|coracoid}}, part of an {{dinogloss|ilium}}, a complete right and [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|distal]] (bottom end) left {{dinogloss|ischium}}, and a complete left {{dinogloss|femur}}. It had been described in 1928 by [[Baron Franz Nopcsa]] as "individual I" in a publication discussing ''Rhabdodon''. Nopcsa had always been fascinated by Albania. Weishampel et al. referred several additional specimens to ''Z. shqiperorum'', some of which were found in isolation or association. These include a left dentary, right and left femur, two ischia, and a [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|proximal]] {{dinogloss|humerus}}, also from the Sanpetru Formation, in addition to a left dentary and partial associated remains of a juvenile individual (including a {{dinogloss|pelvis}} associated with dorsal, {{dinogloss|sacrals|sacral}}, and {{dinogloss|caudals|caudal}} vertebrae) from the [[Densuș-Ciula Formation]]. In the years following the initial description of ''Zalmoxes shqiperorum'' by Weishampel and colleagues in 2003, several other publications described new fossils that they referred to this species, often without confident association of the material or overlap with the holotype. Several authors proposed modified or updated diagnoses for this species based on these new anatomical insights. === Naming === In 2026, [[Susannah Maidment]] and colleagues described a new partial skull from the [[Csehbánya Formation]] of Hungary referable to ''[[Ajkaceratops kozmai]]'', a putative [[ceratopsia]]n dinosaur whose identity as a member of this clade had been debated in the years prior. Using these new remains, the authors reanalyzed ''Ajkaceratops'' in the context of ceratopsian evolution in Europe. They recognized that the holotype of ''Zalmoxes shqiperorum'' could confidently be reidentified as part of a distinct lineage of European ceratopsians, including ''Ajkaceratops''. Since the [[phylogenetic]] placement of ''Z. robustus'' was less stable than ''Z. shqiperorum'', and in some analyses remained an iguanodont close to ''Rhabodon'', Maidment et al. opted to give the new [[Genus|generic name]] ''Ferenceratops'' to "''Z.''" ''shqiperorum''. This name is derived from Ferenc, which is the [[birth name]] of [[Baron Franz Nopcsa]], a notable Hungarian palaeontologist whose work included the study of Haţeg Basin dinosaurs, including the holotype of this species. This is combined with the [[Greek language|Greek]] "ceratops", a common suffix for ceratopsian names, derived from {{wikt-lang|grc|κέρας}} ({{lang|grc-Latn|kéras}}), meaning "horn" and {{wikt-lang|grc|ὤψ}} ({{lang|grc-Latn|ṓps}}), meaning "face". Maidment et al. (2026) only recognized UBB SPZ-2, a referred pelvis, as a suitable referred specimen of ''Ferenceratops'', given the identical anatomy of the ischia. As figured by Weishampel et al. (2003) (then unnumbered), this specimen comprises the nearly complete left and right parts of the pelvis, articulated with {{dinogloss|sacrum}}. As much of the remaining referred material does not overlap with the holotype and needs more thorough study, it was not considered referable to this genus. Since many {{gloss|rhabdodontid}} species are known from material collected [[bone bed]]s, there is often a possibility that the material actually belongs to multiple distinct taxa, with some deriving from iguanodonts and others from ceratopsians. == Description == [[File:Ferenceratops shqiperorum.png|thumb|Speculative [[life restoration]]]] In their 2026 reassessment of ''Ferenceratops'', Maidment and colleagues diagnosed ''F. shqiperorum'' with a unique combination of anatomical characters that distinguished it from other taxa. These include a {{dinogloss|scapula}} that is narrow, with a strap-like blade, expansion at the end, and a prominent, upwardly concave {{dinogloss|acromion|acromial process}} (articulation point for the {{dinogloss|clavicle}}. The {{dinogloss|coracoid}} has a very long, slender sternal process projecting below the bottom margin of the {{dinogloss|glenoid}} (articulation point for the {{dinogloss|humerus}}, forming the shoulder joint). Finally, the {{dinogloss|ischium}} is gently curved and does not have an {{dinogloss|obturator process}}. The authors emphasized that no ornithopod [[synapomorphies]] could be identified in the ''F. shqiperorum'' holotype, and several features are much more consistent with ceratopsians. In ceratopsians, the sternal process of the coracoid is often long and prominent, but it is usually smaller in ornithopods. The absence of an obturator process of the ischium is unsurprising for a ceratopsian but contrasts with ornithopods, where it is a ubiquitous feature. The ilium of a specimen referred to ''Ferenceratops'' is transversely broad, with a sinuous lateral margin when seen from the top or bottom. This is expected for ceratopsians, but not non-[[hadrosaurid]] ornithopods (which {{gloss|rhabdodontids}} have traditionally been regarded as). == Classification == The holotype of ''Ferenceratops'' (previously "''Zalmoxes''") ''shqiperorum'' has traditionally been regarded as belonging to an [[ornithopod]], specifically a member of the [[Rhabdodontidae]]. This is reflected by various earlier [[phylogenetic]] studies. In their 2003 description of ''Zalmoxes'', Weishampel and colleagues recovered the relationships displayed in '''Topology A''' below, with [[heterodontosaurid]]s, [[hypsilophodontid]]s, and [[thescelosaurid]]s as the earliest-diverging members of the Ornithopoda, followed by a small Rhabdodontidae clade (''[[Rhabdodon]]'' + ''Zalmoxes'' spp.) [[Sister group|sister]] to [[Iguanodontia]]. Subsequent research, novel discoveries, and revised anatomical interpretations through the subsequent years allowed for more detailed interpretations of ornithopod (and [[ornithischia]]n, more broadly) relationships. In 2024, Fonseca et al. comprehensively reanalyzed the interrelationships of early ornithischians, with a phylogenetic dataset incorporating most named rhabdodontids at that time, including both ''Zalmoxes'' species. (2026) used the phylogenetic dataset of Han et al. (2017), which was used to test the relationships of the early ceratopsian ''[[Yinlong]]''. Their results confidently placed these genera within the Ceratopsia. The authors explained that the teeth, jaws, and limbs of iguanodontians and ceratopsians are highly [[Convergent evolution|convergent]] in many respects, due to their convergent complex chewing mechanisms, body size, and locomotion. As such, previous work was not suited to recognize the ceratopsian affinities of some {{gloss|rhabdodontids}}. In their extended [[implied weighting]] analysis, the interrelationships of [[Primitive (phylogenetics)|derived]] members of Ceratopsia were poorly resolved, but a distinction between [[marginocephalia]]ns and ornithopods was recovered, with early ornithopod relationships well-resolved. Using a [[Bayesian analysis]], Ceratopsia was fully resolved, with ''Ajkaceratops'', ''Ferenceratops'', and ''Zalmoxes robustus'' forming a distinct clade as the [[sister taxon]] to one including ''[[Zuniceratops]]'', ''[[Turanoceratops]]'', and the more derived [[Ceratopsidae]]. This tree, however, recovered an unresolved [[polytomy]] at the base of [[Cerapoda]], including [[Pachycephalosauria]], [[Ceratopsia]], and most included ornithopod taxa. }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }}|label1=[[Neoceratopsia]]}} == Palaeoecology == [[File:Hatzegopteryx.png|thumb|Paleoenvironmental reconstruction of the giant azhdarchid ''[[Hatzegopteryx]]'' preying on ''Zalmoxes'' (depicted as an ornithopod)]] ''Ferenceratops'' is known from remains found in the [[Sânpetru Formation|Sânpetru]] and [[Densuș-Ciula Formation|Densuș-Ciula]] formations of Romania, both of which preserve the [[Hațeg Island]] biota, which date to the [[Maastrichtian]] age of the late [[Cretaceous]] period. The climate of this paleoenvironment has been interpreted as [[subtropical]], with [[palaeosol]]s (ancient soil layers), flora types, and [[stable isotope]]s indicating fluctuating [[Wet season|rainy]] and [[dry season]]s. [[Carbon isotopes]] imply the conditions were consistent with a {{gloss|dry woodland}}. A mean annual temperature between {{convert|20|and|25|°C|°F}} is suggested by [[oxygen isotopes]]. Both formations are characterized by [[titanosauria]]n sauropods (such as ''[[Magyarosaurus]]'', ''[[Paludititan]]'', ''[[Petrustitan]]'', and ''[[Uriash]]'') and feathered [[theropod]]s ([[dromaeosaurids]], [[troodontids]], ''[[Balaur bondoc|Balaur]]'', and ''[[Elopteryx]]''). Other dinosaurs from the Sânpetru Formation include the [[ankylosaur]] ''[[Struthiosaurus]]'' and the [[hadrosauromorph]] ''[[Telmatosaurus]]''. Other animals of the fauna include the giant [[azhdarchid]] pterosaur ''[[Hatzegopteryx]]'', various [[mesoeucrocodylia]]ns (''[[Allodaposuchus]]'', ''[[ Acynodon]]'', ''[[Doratodon]]'', and ''[[Musturzabalsuchus]]''), various snakes, lizards, and turtles, birds, [[multituberculate]] mammals, [[albanerpetontid]] and [[Frog|anuran]] (frogs) amphibians, and several fish. == See also == * ''[[Ajkaceratops]]'' * [[Timeline of ceratopsian research]] * [[2026 in archosaur paleontology]] == References == {{Reflist |refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Maidment |first1=Susannah C.
